records.title: Bessent announces Argentina fully repaid the $20 billion swap line — only $2.5 billion ever drawn — at a profit to the US taxpayer.
records.text: Bessent announces Argentina fully repaid the $20 billion swap line — only $2.5 billion ever drawn — at a profit to the US taxpayer. The ESF play worked: the peso held, Milei won, and the Treasury banked the carry. The empire's carrot, returned with interest.

records.text: New president Paz issues the Decreto por la Patria — national economic emergency, fuel subsidies gone overnight, prices doubling. The fiscal prelude to killing the peg. When the dollars run out, the decrees get biblical names.

records.text: Three days after the IMF approves a $20 billion program, Argentina dismantles the cepo: free dollar purchases, profit repatriation, the peso in a crawling band. Fourteen years of capital controls end in a weekend.

records.title: The Lower House passes the bill moving crypto into the securities law — insider-trading bans, issuer disclosure, the ETF path, harsher penalties for unlicensed operators.
records.text: The Lower House passes the bill moving crypto into the securities law — insider-trading bans, issuer disclosure, the ETF path, harsher penalties for unlicensed operators. Cabinet approved it April 10; the Upper House vote is still pending. Japan is one vote away from treating crypto like stocks.

records.title: Progmat's consortium launches a forty-institution working group — the megabanks, Nomura, BlackRock Japan, State Street — to tokenize JGBs and put the $1.6 trillion repo market on-chain with …
records.text: Progmat's consortium launches a forty-institution working group — the megabanks, Nomura, BlackRock Japan, State Street — to tokenize JGBs and put the $1.6 trillion repo market on-chain with same-day settlement, live target end of 2026. The register of Japan's own debt heads for the ledger, the same move the DTC made in Washington.

records.title: The Financial System Council's working group publishes its report: move crypto out of the Payment Services Act and into the FIEA, the securities law.
records.text: The Financial System Council's working group publishes its report: move crypto out of the Payment Services Act and into the FIEA, the securities law. Insider-trading bans, issuer disclosure, an ETF path. The paper trail runs back to the FSA's April discussion paper — Japan spent 2025 deciding that crypto is capital markets, not payments.
